## ADR-080(b) trigger evaluation — recorded

ADR-080's revisit trigger (b) fired at SEED-11 (2026-10-01, recorded in the
ADR's own trigger-evaluation note): P31.13 added three CCOPS jurisdictions
and this row was named to answer whether the `government_mandated_disclosure`
extractor class **generalises or splits**.

**Evidence.** This row put nine further sources on the same connector — five
CCOPS municipalities (index→document for St. Louis + Dayton; direct
`disclosure_document` rows for Columbia's annual report, Anchorage's AO
2023-78 ordinance text and Austin's TRUST resolution) and four district
self-disclosure pages — using only reviewed ADAPTER DATA: the existing
`index_page`/`disclosure_document` kinds, `technology_field_multi` (the
P31.13 combined-filing key), and two additive reviewed keys
(`period_from_capture`, `field_patterns[].claim_type`/`value`). No new
extractor code path entered the class; the agency-policy publishers are NOT
a split of the disclosure connector — they are a separate `agency_policy`
connector over the shared OKC clause machinery, exactly the boundary
ADR-080 drew (the disclosure class stays per-agency-aggregate; the policy
class emits clause facts, never deployment claims).

**Outcome: reaffirm-as-is.** The class generalised. The trigger's premise —
that breadth pressure would force a split — did not materialise: the
guards (`disclosure_claim` genre/predicate/aggregate + Part VIII) bind
every new row identically, the genre gate still refuses use claims on
policy-document filings, and the aggregate schema is unchanged. No new ADR
is filed; ADR-080's body is never edited (SIG-ENG-003). The unanswered
clause — (a) a CCOPS jurisdiction shipping a machine-readable inventory —
remains open for future rounds.
